newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton extends losses as new crops come in.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton extends losses as new crops come in.

text.p: Indian cotton prices extended losses on Friday as new crops started coming into the market, dealers said.

"Mill demand was low while reports of rising new crop arrivals at producing centres prompted fresh offerings," one dealer said. Reports that the government had allowed export of 150,000 bales (170 kg each) of Bengal-deshi cotton failed to lift the market.
In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan fell by 100 rupees to 13,200/13,500 per candy (355.56 kg). Bengal-deshi ready delivery eased by 20 rupees to 820/840 per maund (37.32 kg)
